text:
Companion Animal Travel Desk minutes for Aurelia Skyways were taken by the shift coordinator. Attendees were Leo Wilson, Arjun Nakamura, and Rosie.

We started with the service flow for pet transfers between skyports. The team reviewed how the ground crew moves carriers with care from one service point to the next, then checks the labels before the next handoff. The main aim is to keep the process calm and clear for travelers and pets alike, with no confusion when the cabin teams take over.

Brightwater names the pet deck where animals travel, and the crew agreed to keep that term consistent in every handoff note. That keeps the desk, the loading staff, and the cabin team using the same wording, which cuts down on mix-ups at the ramp and in customer updates.

Windmere names the person who handles pets on board, and the team said that role has to be flagged clearly on every case file. The group also agreed that any passenger concern gets a quick answer from the desk before boarding, so nobody is left guessing about a carrier, a leash, or a handoff.

Leo Wilson raised a concern about a tight connection and wanted a cleaner update path. Arjun Nakamura asked for a shorter check-in script so passengers hear the important points first. Rosie was discussed as a reminder that pet comfort matters during every transfer, not just at the start and finish. We agreed to keep the tone calm, keep instructions short, and pass along any special notes without delay.

The final check focused on handoff timing, carrier placement, and how the desk records each step for the next team. I reminded everyone that the Companion Animal Travel Desk works best when we stick to one clear process and avoid extra chatter. The crew was in agreement that the next shift should keep the same pace and keep customers informed from start to finish.

The meeting ended.
